series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

verdict.text: Brazil submitted its First NDC adjustment (2023) on 2023-10-27; no numeric target has been extracted from it. A later submission, Second Nationally Determined Contribution, was filed on 2024-11-13; it has not been read, so no figure here comes from it. 73 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (27). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 2804.4 MtCO₂e, DS-02 1167.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 3 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 50.7 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: Reduce GHG emissions by 37% in 2025, and by 43% (indicative) in 2030 below 2005 levels It was classed unconditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.15°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4.49°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
